topic: Algae: Major Groups, Characteristics and Examples
title: Green, Brown or Red Algae? Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
Green slime on a water tank, brown seaweed on the seashore and a wobbly jelly in a cup all come from algae. Diya sees the slime on her water tank wall and asks: is this slime a plant? This lesson covers algae, the simplest members of the plant kingdom, from NCERT Class 11 Biology, Chapter 3.

You will see what makes an alga (chlorophyll, a thallus body, mostly water homes) and a live zoom ladder that takes the tank slime down to a filament, one cell with its spiral chloroplast, and the pyrenoids. We compare forms (Volvox, Ulothrix, Spirogyra, kelps), run the three ways algae reproduce (fragmentation, zoospores, gametes fusing), compare isogamous and oogamous reproduction, and build NCERT Table 3.1 row by row for Chlorophyceae, Phaeophyceae and Rhodophyceae: pigments, stored food, cell wall, flagella and habitat. Then uses of algae (food, agar), a worked example sorting six algae, the exam trap about chlorophyll, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 22 of our PUC Biology series.
Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and NEET students.
